parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Find the probability that a score of 3 is obtained for the first time on the 8th spin.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Find the probability that fewer than 6 spins are required to obtain a score of 3 for the first time.

text: A fair spinner with 5 sides numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 is spun repeatedly. The score on each spin is the
number on the side on which the spinner lands.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Find the probability that on a randomly chosen day Georgie wears a hat.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Find the probability that on a randomly chosen day Georgie wears a yellow scarf given that she
does not wear a hat.

text: Georgie has a red scarf, a blue scarf and a yellow scarf. Each day she wears exactly one of these
scarves. The probabilities for the three colours are 0.2, 0.45 and 0.35 respectively. When she wears a
red scarf, she always wears a hat. When she wears a blue scarf, she wears a hat with probability 0.4.
When she wears a yellow scarf, she wears a hat with probability 0.3.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Find the probability that a shopper chosen at random spends between 85 and 100 minutes in the
shopping centre. 
88% of shoppers spend more than t minutes in the shopping centre.

text: The time spent by shoppers in a large shopping centre has a normal distribution with mean 96 minutes
and standard deviation 18 minutes.

parts.text: Draw up the probability distribution table for X, in terms of k.

text: The random variable X takes the values 1, 2, 3, 4 only. The probability that X takes the value x is
kx�5 − x, where k is a constant.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Draw a cumulative frequency graph to illustrate the data.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
For 30% of these journeys the distance travelled is d km or more.
Use your graph to estimate the value of d.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Calculate an estimate of the mean distance travelled for the 150 journeys.

text: A driver records the distance travelled in each of 150 journeys. These distances, correct to the nearest
km, are summarised in the following table.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Find the total number of different arrangements of the 11 letters in the word CATERPILLAR.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Find the total number of different arrangements of the 11 letters in the word CATERPILLAR in
which there is an R at the beginning and an R at the end, and the two As are not together.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Find the total number of different selections of 6 letters from the 11 letters of the word
CATERPILLAR that contain both Rs and at least one A and at least one L.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Find the probability that the student prefers swimming.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Determine whether the events ‘the student is male’ and ‘the student prefers swimming’ are
independent, justifying your answer. 
On average at all the schools in this country 30% of the students do not like any sports.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
10 of the students from this country are chosen at random.
Find the probability that at least 3 of these students do not like any sports.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
90 students from this country are now chosen at random.
Use an approximation to find the probability that fewer than 32 of them do not like any
sports.
